scams.name: Oaxaca Mezcal Tour Commission Kickback & 'Artisanal' Quality Fraud
scams.description: Oaxaca is Mexico's mezcal capital and 'Ruta del Mezcal' (Santiago Matatlán area) day tours are among the city's most-popular experiences — but 2025 community coverage documents a commission-kickback ecosystem targeting tourists. Community threads on mezcal tastings, first-time Oaxaca itineraries, and ethical tourism consistently surface the same patterns. The 2025 scams: (a) Alcalá pedestrian-strip touts selling 'exclusive mezcal tour MX$1,800' when the legitimate small-group operator rate is MX$800–$1,200; (b) tours visiting only 2 palenques (promised 4–5) with padded time at the 'family friend' palenque charging MX$400+ for bottles worth MX$200–$300; (c) 'Premium añejo bottle special MX$2,500' pressured at palenque — this is a standard 3-year añejo that retails MX$800–$1,200 at Oaxaca City specialty shops; (d) 'Worm bottle' or 'gusano' premium — the worm (actually a moth larva) is a marketing gimmick, not a quality indicator — real artisanal mezcal does NOT contain a worm; (e) fake 'Denominación de Origen' certified labels on unlicensed palenque output. Community reports document the broader Oaxaca tourist-commission pattern. For older travelers: (1) book ONLY through reputable small-group operators with published Google 4.7+ reviews: Coyote Aventuras, Experience Mezcal, Mezcoaxaca, or El Destilado direct — MX$800–$1,200 per person 6-hour tour to 4 palenques; (2) CONFIRM the palenques being visited in writing AND check each one is a Denominación de Origen certified producer (list at crm.mx); (3) REFUSE worm-bottle 'premium' purchases — real artisanal mezcal is worm-free; (4) fair bottle prices at legitimate palenques: joven MX$400–$700, reposado MX$600–$1,000, añejo MX$800–$1,500 — anything MX$2,500+ should have provable aging certification; (5) buy in Oaxaca City at Mezcaloteca (Reforma 506) or Mezcalería In Situ (Reforma 602) with transparent pricing and expert staff; (6) pace tastings — 4 palenques × 4 tastings = 16 shots, older travelers should limit to 8–10 sips total; (7) eat substantial meals before/during; (8) NEVER drive yourself after mezcal tastings — check-points in Oaxaca valley enforce DUI.
scams.avoidance: Book Coyote Aventuras, Experience Mezcal, or Mezcoaxaca (Google 4.7+) CONFIRM specific palenques in writing; verify D.O. certification REFUSE worm bottles; fair añejo price MX$800–$1,500 not MX$2,500+ Buy in-city at Mezcaloteca or Mezcalería In Situ with transparent pricing Pace yourself: 16 shots across 4 palenques is too much for most
scams.location: Santiago Matatlán (Mezcal Route) palenques, Teotitlán del Valle combined tour stops, Mitla-approach tasting rooms, Oaxaca City Alcalá tout clusters

scams.name: Oaxaca Monte Albán / Mitla Combined Tour Overcharge & Commission Stops
scams.description: The 'Combined Valley Tour' (Monte Albán + Mitla + Tule Tree + Teotitlán weavers + mezcal palenque) is Oaxaca's flagship day-trip and hosts a 2025 commission-kickback ecosystem at each stop. Community reports consistently document the day-trip structure across 2025 threads. The 2025 scams: (a) Alcalá pedestrian-strip operators selling 'full valley tour MX$1,500' that's a group-share of 15+ tourists in a cramped van with only 45 min at each site; (b) 'private tour MX$4,000 per person' that's actually identical to the MX$1,500 group tour with added commission stops; (c) Teotitlán 'rug factory visit' where master weavers' demos are genuine but the shop pressure for MX$12,000–$35,000 rugs is aggressive — fair prices for 6×9 ft hand-loomed wool with natural dyes are MX$6,000–$18,000; (d) Monte Albán 'mandatory guide MX$400 per person' at entrance — no guide is required; self-guided maps are free; licensed optional guides charge MX$200–$350 PER GROUP; (e) 'traditional embroidery' demo at commission stops with MX$2,000 'village women' shirt pricing vs MX$400–$800 at Mercado de Abastos; (f) Tule Tree 'entrance donation MX$50' at an unofficial 'donation box' run by touts (official entry is MX$10). Community reports document the broader 2025 commission pattern. For older travelers: (1) book ONLY through Google 4.7+ operators with published itineraries: Horus Tours Oaxaca, Coyote Aventuras, Oaxacking, or Fundación En Vía — MX$700–$1,200 per person small-group tour (max 8 people); (2) Monte Albán entry is MX$95 for foreigners; NO mandatory guide — licensed optional guides are MX$200–$350 PER GROUP; (3) at Teotitlán, browse without pressure; fair rug price is MX$1,200–$2,500 per square metre of hand-loomed natural-dye wool; haggle 20–30% from opening; (4) at Tule Tree, official entry is MX$10 — ignore MX$50 'donations' at unofficial tables; (5) bring Rp... err, MX$500 small bills for entries (Monte Albán MX$95 + Mitla MX$95 + Tule MX$10 + meal MX$250); (6) most valleys tours pack too much into one day; consider splitting Monte Albán (half-day) and Mitla-Teotitlán (separate half-day); (7) own driver via Didi/Uber from Oaxaca to Monte Albán is MX$200–$300 each way (vs MX$1,500 tour if you only want the ruins).
scams.avoidance: Book Horus Tours, Coyote Aventuras, or Oaxacking (Google 4.7+, max 8 pax) Monte Albán: MX$95 entry, NO mandatory guide; optional MX$200–$350/GROUP Teotitlán rugs: fair MX$1,200–$2,500/sq metre; haggle 20–30% Tule Tree official entry MX$10 — ignore MX$50 'donations' For ruins only, Uber/Didi MX$200–$300 each way; skip tour
scams.location: Monte Albán UNESCO site, Mitla archaeological zone, Tule Tree stop, Teotitlán del Valle weavers, El Tule artisan commission shops

scams.name: Oaxaca Pasillo de Humo / Food Market 'Tourist Menu' Overcharge Scam
scams.description: The Mercado 20 de Noviembre 'Pasillo de Humo' (Smoke Passage) — where diners pick raw meat and local vendors grill it to order — is Oaxaca's most-iconic food experience. Community reports document a specific 2025 tourist-overcharge experience, with practical how-to guides explaining how Pasillo de Humo works. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) carniceros (butchers) selling raw meat to tourists at 2–3x the local rate (beef tasajo MX$380/kg to tourist vs MX$180/kg to local; chorizo MX$350/kg vs MX$150/kg); (b) grill vendors charging MX$80 'cooking fee per plate' not disclosed upfront; (c) 'tortillas + salsas + drinks' bundled at MX$180/person (real cost MX$30); (d) Alcalá pedestrian-strip tourist-menu restaurants with MX$500+ mole negro entries (real mercado mole negro is MX$150–$200); (e) Zócalo 'traditional Oaxacan' restaurants with surprise credit-card surcharges 8–12%; (f) pre-written bills for 'amount of food we think you ate' rather than itemised receipts. Community threads cover the broader 2025 Oaxaca food-scene context. For older travelers: (1) at Pasillo de Humo, ASK prices BEFORE the butcher starts cutting — fair tasajo is MX$150–$200/kg (you buy ~150g per person = MX$25–$30); fair chorizo MX$120–$150/kg; (2) for the grill, fair 'cooking fee' is MX$30–$50 per plate, tortillas/salsas MX$20 total for a couple; (3) total fair Pasillo meal for two: MX$150–$200 (not MX$500+); (4) walk around and watch prices locals are paying BEFORE ordering; (5) at market restaurants, order ONLY from a POSTED written menu with prices — refuse 'seasonal' quoted-only items; (6) for reliable Oaxacan food at fair prices, try Casa Oaxaca Café (Constitución 104), Zandunga (García Vigil 512), or Criollo (Francisco I Madero 129) — all Google 4.7+ with transparent pricing MX$250–$450 per person for full meal; (7) CONFIRM credit-card surcharge policy at check-in — should be 0–3%; some Oaxaca Zócalo restaurants add 8–12% without notice; (8) bring small-bill cash (MX$50, 100, 200) to avoid 'no change' pressure at markets.
scams.avoidance: ASK prices BEFORE butcher cuts; fair tasajo MX$150–$200/kg Total fair Pasillo meal for two: MX$150–$200 Watch locals paying before you order; ignore tourist lines Eat at Casa Oaxaca Café, Zandunga, or Criollo — transparent MX$250–$450 Confirm credit-card surcharge 0–3% max BEFORE ordering
scams.location: Mercado 20 de Noviembre 'Pasillo de Humo' (Smoke Passage), Mercado Benito Juárez, Zócalo tourist-menu restaurants, Alcalá pedestrian-strip comedores

scams.name: Oaxaca Airport (OAX) Taxi & Hotel-Transfer Overcharge
scams.description: Oaxaca Xoxocotlán Airport (OAX) is small (12 km from Centro Histórico, 20 min drive) but hosts a thin taxi-overcharge pattern. Community reports discuss arrival logistics and the baseline taxi-legitimacy question consistently. The legitimate fares: OAX airport to Centro Histórico (12 km) is MX$180–$250 via Uber/Didi; the official Transporte Terrestre (airport-authorized sedan) is MX$220–$280 flat-rate prepaid at the booth. Collective van (combi) to Centro is MX$60–$75 per person (30 min with stops). The 2025 scams: (a) arrivals-kerb 'taxi' sign-holders quoting MX$500–$800 (2–3x real rate); (b) 'Hotel transfer VIP' claimed at MX$1,200 for a standard sedan ride; (c) private driver insisting 'Uber doesn't work here' — Uber IS available in Oaxaca with 5–15 min wait; (d) 'combined airport + Monte Albán tour package' bait bundled at MX$2,000 with excuse 'already booked'; (e) Didi cancellation scam — same pattern as documented in Mexico City community reports; (f) hotel-side bellhop kickbacks directing guests to 'recommended driver' at 1.8x rate. For older travelers: (1) book Uber or Didi on airport Wi-Fi AFTER luggage — typical fare MX$180–$250 for the 20-min ride to Centro; (2) if Uber is slow, the official Transporte Terrestre booth inside arrivals IS legitimate at MX$220–$280 flat-rate prepaid (look for uniformed staff + printed receipts); (3) the combi (shared van) to Centro is MX$60–$75 per person — cheap budget option; (4) IGNORE every 'taxi' sign-holder at arrivals kerb quoting MX$500+; (5) your hotel likely includes free airport pickup with advance email — use this; (6) for return to OAX, pre-book Uber or the night before at Rp ... err MX$180–$250 from Centro; (7) Oaxaca is compact — once in Centro Histórico, most sights are walkable; use Uber for evening returns to hotel if dining far out; (8) save Oaxaca Tourist Police: +52 951 501 5000 ext. 23406 (English available).
scams.avoidance: Book Uber/Didi on airport Wi-Fi — MX$180–$250 to Centro (20 min) Official Transporte Terrestre booth inside arrivals IS legit (MX$220–$280) Budget: combi shared van MX$60–$75 per person (30 min) Use hotel's free airport pickup (advance email booking) Oaxaca Tourist Police English: +52 951 501 5000 ext. 23406
scams.location: Xoxocotlán International Airport (OAX) arrivals, Sitio Taxi kiosks, ADO bus-station taxi queue, Centro Histórico hotel drop-offs

scams.name: Oaxaca Día de los Muertos / Guelaguetza Festival Price-Gouging & Airbnb Cancellations
scams.description: Oaxaca's Día de los Muertos (Oct 28 – Nov 3) and Guelaguetza festival (July) are Mexico's most-iconic cultural celebrations — and host 2025 price-gouging + booking-cancellation scams. Community reports document specific 2025 cancellation scams, and English event guides for first-time solo visitors give useful planning baselines. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) Airbnb cancellation + re-list at 3–5x price — hosts cancel confirmed bookings made 6+ months ahead (without compensation), relist same property at MX$8,000–$15,000 per night for the Día festival window; (b) 'exclusive rooftop viewing package' sold at MX$3,500 per person for the Zócalo parades (which are free public events visible from any sidewalk); (c) 'VIP cemetery tour Xoxocotlán MX$2,500' when public cemetery visits are free and local tours cost MX$400–$600; (d) fake 'festival parade ticket' resellers on WhatsApp selling non-existent 'front-row' access; (e) restaurants posting 'festival menu' at 2–3x normal prices with MX$1,200 mole negro; (f) 'official comparsa dancer photo session' at MX$500 per photo — these are local community members, not professional performers; tipping MX$50–$100 at their discretion is fair. For older travelers: (1) book accommodations 9–12 MONTHS ahead of Día de los Muertos (Oct 28 – Nov 3) via Booking.com, Hyatt, or Marriott directly — platform-protected bookings have recourse against cancellation scams; (2) Airbnb cancellation has limited recourse — community reports document specific cancelled-booking cases; prefer hotel chains for guaranteed booking; (3) REFUSE every 'exclusive rooftop viewing package' and 'VIP cemetery tour' — the parades and cemeteries are FREE PUBLIC events; (4) for a guided Día experience, book ONLY via reputable English-speaking operators (Horus Tours, Coyote Aventuras) at MX$600–$1,000; (5) budget for festival-surcharge meals (restaurants legitimately raise 20–30% during Día); skip the MX$1,200 mole negro; (6) bring plenty of small bills for vendor tipping (MX$50–$100 to performers is generous); (7) respect altars and graveside rituals — photograph from distance, ask permission for close shots; (8) plan to arrive Oct 26–27 and depart Nov 4–5 for full festival without peak-price crush.
scams.avoidance: Book accommodations 9–12 months ahead via Booking.com/Hyatt/Marriott REFUSE 'exclusive rooftop' and 'VIP cemetery tour' — events are FREE Guided Día experience: Horus Tours or Coyote Aventuras MX$600–$1,000 Airbnb Día has high cancellation risk — prefer hotel chains Arrive Oct 26–27, depart Nov 4–5 to avoid peak-price crush
scams.location: Oaxaca Centro Histórico hotels/Airbnbs Oct 28 – Nov 3 (Día de los Muertos), July (Guelaguetza), Xoxocotlán cemetery tours, 'exclusive rooftop' viewing packages

scams.name: Oaxaca Rental-Car Card-Cloning & Mitla-Approach Highway Scam
scams.description: Oaxaca rental-car agencies have a documented 2025 credit-card cloning + deposit-refusal pattern. Community reports document the pattern consistently and cover the broader 2025 tourist-targeting context. The highway variant mirrors Yucatán's 'Mi Lindo Yucatán' pattern documented in Chichén Itzá area reports. The 2025 scams: (a) rental-car 'security deposit MX$8,000–$15,000' charged to credit card — deposit is either 'held' for 30–60 days (accruing interest + foreign fees) or never refunded; (b) fake 'pre-existing damage' claims on vehicle return — dent or scratch that wasn't photographed at pickup; (c) Mitla-approach 'highway restaurant' tourist-trap where drivers are directed to stop — 2–3x restaurant prices + commission to driver; (d) 'required insurance' upsold at MX$800/day on top of base rate — most US and Canadian credit cards include rental insurance for Mexico (verify yours); (e) 'mandatory toll fee MX$400' added at return (tolls on Route 190 are legitimate but max MX$80–$120 each way); (f) unlicensed 'budget rental' agencies on Alcalá street that don't accept insurance documents. For older travelers: (1) book rental cars ONLY via verified agencies with Google 4.5+ reviews (Hertz Oaxaca, Europcar, Budget, Expedia Cars) at the AIRPORT not city offices; (2) photograph EVERY scratch, dent, tire condition, mileage BEFORE driving off — timestamp all photos; require an inspection form signed by the agent; (3) verify your credit card's rental insurance coverage in Mexico BEFORE declining agency insurance (MX$800/day is significant); (4) REFUSE 'security deposit' above US$500; if required, use a credit card WITH dispute protection — never debit card; (5) on the Mitla-approach route 190, DO NOT stop at any restaurant the driver 'recommends' — eat in Mitla or Teotitlán at Google 4.5+ verified spots; (6) keep ALL toll receipts to verify final charges; legitimate tolls on Route 190 Oaxaca–Tehuantepec are MX$60–$120 each way; (7) consider Uber/Didi between city and valley sites instead of rental car — MX$250–$400 each way is often cheaper and zero-risk; (8) if defrauded, file denuncia at Oaxaca MP (+52 951 514 3822) within 48 hours for chargeback documentation.
scams.avoidance: Book verified agencies (Hertz, Europcar, Budget) at AIRPORT only Photograph every scratch/tire/mileage BEFORE driving off (timestamped) Verify credit-card rental insurance in Mexico BEFORE declining Refuse security deposits above US$500; credit card only (dispute-able) On Route 190, don't stop at 'recommended' restaurants; eat in Mitla
scams.location: Oaxaca City rental-car offices (airport + Alcalá), Mitla-approach Route 190, Teotitlán turnoff highway, 'highway restaurant' stops on valley tour route
